text:
University of Pittsburgh Athletics
10/27/2026 9:48:00 AM
|
General, Men's Basketball
Share:
PITTSBURGH
- Pitt Athletics and its multimedia rights holder JMI Sports today announced a multiyear partnership with Gecko Robotics, a global leader in AI-powered robotics founded in Pittsburgh, that will bring the company's logo to Pitt Men's Basketball jerseys beginning in the 2026-27 season.

The agreement marks the first jersey patch partner for Pitt Men's Basketball and will debut when Pitt hosts Rider in the regular season opener on Monday, Nov. 2, at the Petersen Events Center.

"Gecko Robotics is a Pittsburgh success story, built on the same ambition and work ethic that define this city and this University," Pitt Director of Athletics
C. Allen Greene
said. "Our strategic plan, The Gold Standard, calls on us to pursue new revenue while building partnerships that fit who we are, and this one does both. Jersey patches are a new chapter in college athletics, and we are proud to have Gecko Robotics, a company that reflects the innovation happening across Pitt and our region, as our first men's basketball partner. This partnership creates meaningful opportunities for our student-athletes and strengthens our connection to Pittsburgh's technology community."

Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Pittsburgh, Gecko Robotics combines AI and robotics to help build, maintain and modernize critical industries worldwide, including defense, energy, oil and gas and manufacturing. Gecko Robotics brings the city's signature grit to solving some of the world's most complex infrastructure challenges.

As such, Gecko Robotics will be a Gold Standard Partner of Pitt Athletics, strengthening the company's continued investment in Pittsburgh's higher education ecosystem as it expands engineering, manufacturing and defense capabilities and jobs in the region.

"Pittsburgh is the city of champions. Gecko was forged here, and we believe in backing winners. We are proud to support Pitt Athletics and its men's basketball program," said Jake Loosararian, CEO and Co-founder of Gecko Robotics. "Pittsburgh and grit go hand in hand. This city has shaped the future before, and now we are doing it again. This partnership represents a new dawn for the city of champions."

Gecko Robotics will also create Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) opportunities for select Pitt Men's Basketball student-athletes in collaboration with H2PNIL, Pitt Athletics' NIL platform. Campaigns will integrate student-athletes into the company's marketing through digital content series and other efforts.

"Our players take great pride in representing Pittsburgh, and having a company founded in this city on our jerseys makes that even more meaningful," said Pitt Head Men's Basketball Coach
Jeff Capel
. "Gecko Robotics is building the future right here at home, and what I appreciate most is that this partnership goes beyond a logo. It gives our young men the chance to connect with leaders in technology and innovation, and we are excited to wear the Gecko patch with pride this season."

JMI Sports, operating locally as Pitt Sports Marketing, worked in collaboration with Pitt Athletics to develop the agreement with Gecko Robotics. In addition to the jersey patch, the partnership includes a range of multimedia assets that will see Gecko Robotics branding and signage at the Petersen Events Center, in addition to in-game recognition at Pitt Men's Basketball home games, digital and social media features, and a series of community engagement opportunities.

"Gecko Robotics is a powerful example of a global company that recognizes the enormous platform of college athletics to advance business priorities and create regional impact," said Paul Archey, President at JMI Sports. "Gecko Robotics' commitment to its hometown's flagship university is an investment in the next generation of talent. We are excited by their ambition to put their support front and center with Pitt Basketball."

ABOUT PITT ATHLETICS

The University of Pittsburgh Department of Athletics sponsors 19 varsity sports and is a proud member of the Atlantic Coast Conference. Committed to excellence in competition, academics and community, Pitt Athletics develops student-athletes who compete at the highest level while preparing them for success beyond sport. For more information, visit pittsburghpanthers.com.

ABOUT GECKO ROBOTICS

Gecko Robotics combines advanced robotics and AI-powered software to build, maintain and modernize the world's most critical infrastructure.

Using robots that climb, crawl, fly and swim, Gecko is able to collect an unprecedented amount of data on the built world, whether that's with Fortune 100 companies in energy, oil and gas, and manufacturing sectors around the world, or the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Navy to protect and optimize nuclear submarines and aircraft carriers.

Through our AI-powered platform, Cantilever, Gecko transforms the massive datasets collected by robots into actionable insights that enable data-driven, evidence-based decisions on structures, delivering an ROI for customers.

ABOUT JMI SPORTS

JMI Sports is a leading media rights and venue development company that provides management of collegiate multimedia rights, sponsorship sales agency representation and project management expertise for the development of collegiate and professional sports facilities. The company serves to maximize each client's economic potential through customized initiatives, from marketing and branding solutions to facility design strategies.

JMI Sports' signature collegiate multimedia rights partnerships include the University of Kentucky, UCLA, the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Pittsburgh, Harvard University, Columbia University, San Diego State University, University of California at San Diego, University of San Diego and joint-venture properties at the University of Georgia (with Learfield) and University of Notre Dame (with Legends). JMI Sports also represents multimedia rights for several conferences, including the Ivy League, the Mid-American Conference, the Mountain West Conference, the Patriot League and the Atlantic 10, and serves as third-party sales representation for premier sports properties, venues and events including Rupp Arena at Central Bank Center, the Rose Bowl, the Penn Relays and USA Volleyball.

JMI Sports was founded in 2006 by CEO Erik Judson and technology entrepreneur John Moores, former owner of the San Diego Padres. To learn more, please visit www.jmisports.com.

attributes.description: Pat Narduzzi puts the Miami loss on himself, breaks down how field position and execution got away from Pitt and looks ahead to a Halloween night showdown wi...

text:
University of Pittsburgh Athletics
10/26/2026 4:46:00 PM
|
Football
Share:
By:
Abby Schnable
Pat Narduzzi
did what he always does after a loss on Monday, and that was to put it on himself.

The Panthers fell at No. 1 Miami, and in the days since, Narduzzi has watched the film, found the details and come away with a clear picture of how the game got away.

The short version is that it was about field position, execution and the thin margin between good enough and great.

Now Pitt turns the page to Georgia Tech, a Saturday night Halloween matchup with two banged-up teams that are both hungry for a win.

Field position set the tone

The film told the story long before the final score did. Pitt's offense went three-and-out on its opening possession, and the punt that followed had a short hang time and landed in the hands of one of the country's top returners.

Narduzzi pointed to that sequence as the first domino, a small mistake against the kind of team that punishes them.

"34 of their points were scored on short fields, 50 yards or less," Narduzzi said. "I don't care who you're playing, you're going to struggle. But we were on the field 20 minutes and 20 seconds in the first half defensively, and you don't give a team that's that explosive the ball."

The Toney problem

Miami's Malachi Toney was the name Pitt's defense kept running into. The Panthers often had two defenders on him, whether a linebacker and a safety or some other bracket. He still found ways to get open, and Narduzzi gave him his due.

The head coach pointed to Toney's head fakes and his feel for manipulating coverage, and he admitted the safety help was sometimes a little deeper than Pitt wanted.

"He's a fantastic football player," Narduzzi said. "He's a Heisman candidate, and we didn't do a good enough job in coverage. Our plan wasn't good enough to stop him, but we did have two guys on him a lot. You're worried about covering him, so you're not worried about being physical. The combination of being physical and getting your hands on him as well as covering him is something that's hard to do."

Sticking with the plan

Pitt tried some different looks against Miami, and Narduzzi was candid that they didn't help.

The Panthers were strong on first and second down for most of the afternoon, but they couldn't get off the field on third down. He also gave credit to Miami's quarterback, calling him accurate and another Heisman candidate on that offense.

That led Narduzzi back to a philosophy he preaches to his players.

He believes a team can tweak its game plan from week to week, but a total overhaul usually backfires, especially in the middle of a season. The message to the locker room is to trust the plan, play fast and make plays.

"You can try a bunch of different things, and we did some different things for sure," Narduzzi said. "But it's got to go within the framework of who you are and what you do. Otherwise, we won't execute it well. I talk to our kids all the time about sticking with the plan. I think the worst teams start to change their plan midseason, then it goes downhill."

Quarterbacks taking a step

Holden Geriner
remains the guy for Pitt, and Narduzzi liked what he saw in the areas the staff wanted him to work on. He stepped up in the pocket and took off running a couple of times, the kind of improvements the coaches had been asking for.

Narduzzi said
Corey Dailey
showed progress too, and he called it a step forward for the whole quarterback room.

"They made major improvements," Narduzzi said. "Is it good enough to win? No. Did we miss some stuff down the field? Yes. And that's, again, it's a process. We'd like to instantly have a guy back there throwing 75% completions, but that's not where we are right now. But we're going to get there. We have confidence in those guys to get it done."

Looking ahead to Georgia Tech

Georgia Tech comes to Pittsburgh on Saturday night, Halloween, with an injury report that Narduzzi said looks a lot like Pitt's.

The Yellow Jackets are coming off a tough outing against Boston College, which means both teams are hungry for a win. He also expects a very different look than last year, when Haynes King made the Georgia Tech offense a dual-threat challenge.

He also tried to widen the lens for his team after the loss. Among Power Four programs, 32 have five or more wins, and Pitt is one of them.

"There are 20 teams in the country that have six or seven wins, and there's 12 that have five wins," Narduzzi said. "We're one of those 12. We've done some great things, dealt with some injuries and not necessarily having all our guns when we walk out on the field. But there's a lot of football to be played, and our goal is to go one and zero each week.

text:
University of Pittsburgh Athletics
Photo by: Pitt Athletics
7/3/2026 1:32:00 PM
|
Football
Share:

PITTSBURGH
—Pitt's rich football tradition was prominently recognized by ESPN in its ranking of the best college football players of all time by jersey number.

The Panthers placed four former standouts on the list, with
Larry Fitzgerald Jr.
,
Tony Dorsett
,
Aaron Donald
and
Hugh Green
each selected as the greatest college football player to wear their respective number.

Fitzgerald Jr. was named the top player to ever wear No. 1 following one of the most spectacular receiving careers in college football history. In just two seasons at Pitt from 2002-03, he caught 161 passes for 2,677 yards and 34 touchdowns. Fitzgerald Jr. won the 2003 Biletnikoff Award and Walter Camp Player of the Year honor, was a unanimous All-American and finished second in the Heisman Trophy voting. His streak of 18 consecutive games with a touchdown reception remains an NCAA record.

Dorsett earned the nod at No. 33 after a legendary Pitt career that culminated with the 1976 Heisman Trophy and national championship. A three-time first-team All-American, Dorsett rushed for 6,082 career yards, setting an NCAA record that stood for 22 years. During his senior season, he powered Pitt to a perfect 12-0 record and the program's ninth national title.

Donald was selected as the greatest No. 97 after one of the most dominant defensive seasons in college football history. As a senior in 2013, Donald swept the nation's major defensive awards, winning the Bronko Nagurski Trophy, Chuck Bednarik Award, Rotary Lombardi Award and Outland Trophy. He led the country with 28.5 tackles for loss and finished his Pitt career with a school-record 66 TFLs.

Green rounded out Pitt's honorees as ESPN's choice for No. 99. One of the most decorated defensive players in college football history, Green was a three-time All-American and the 1980 recipient of the Maxwell Award, Walter Camp Award and Rotary Lombardi Award. He finished second in the 1980 Heisman Trophy voting, the highest finish ever by a strictly defensive player.

Pitt was also represented among ESPN's additional selections, with
Dan Marino
listed among the top players to wear No. 13,
Mark May
among No. 73,
Jimbo Covert
among No. 75,
Bill Fralic
among No. 79,
Antonio Bryant
among No. 80,
Mike Ditka
among No. 89 and
Joe Schmidt
among No. 65.

The full ESPN
list
ranked the top college football player for every jersey number from 0 through 99.

text:
John Altdorfer

Chatham Announces Wrestling Programs, Athletic Alley, Purple & Gray Club

02.06.25

Share:

Story Links

PITTSBURGH -
On Thursday, Chatham University doubled-down on its commitment to the development of athletics with the announcement of Men's and Women's Wrestling, Athletic Alley and the Purple & Gray Club.

"I am delighted to share exciting news about Chatham's continued growth and commitment to further activating Chatham Eastside, enhancing student life, supporting athletic excellence, and fostering community engagement," said Dr. Rhonda Phillps, Chatham President.

Wrestling Programs

Vice President of Athletics and Recreation
Leonard Trevino
has announced the addition of Men's and Women's Wrestling as the school's 24th and 25th intercollegiate programs.

These programs, which join Women's Flag Football and Competitive Cheer as recent additions to Chatham, are set to begin competition in the fall of 2026.

"The addition of these programs continues the positive trajectory of athletics at Chatham University," shared Trevino. "We are excited to add these two sports and are committed to support and build competitive wrestling programs. We will begin a nationwide search for both a head Men's Wrestling and a head Women's Wrestling coach."

Athletic Alley

In conjunction with these new programs, Chatham is also unveiling the plan for "Athletic Alley", which aims to serve as a hub for athletics, health & wellness and community engagement at Chatham's Eastside campus.

Amenities to be featured at Athletic Alley include:

A designated wrestling practice room, which will serve the new programs, and a multi-purpose room, which will serve competitive cheer and can be utilized by all teams.

A state-of-the-art weight room/training facility specifically designed to meet the needs of Chatham's athletic programs, while being inviting to the general population.

Locker rooms, which will benefit teams and general users at Eastside. They are scheduled for the 2026-27 school year.

Batting cages and a bullpen area, which will aid Chatham's Baseball and Softball programs.

Purple & Gray Club

In an effort to further develop athletics and enhance student experience, Chatham has announced the founding of the
Purple & Gray Club
, which will financially support the Athletic Alley project and future athletic initiatives.

"Our student-athletes have found great success both on the field of play and in the classroom, and we invite you to help us continue our investment in our student-athletes," said Trevino.

To join Chatham Athletics in building an exciting and inspiring future, contact Doug Caputo at 412-365-1262 or d.caputo@chatham.edu or
Leonard Trevino
at 412-365-1650.

Agreement places a UPMC patch on Pitt Football jerseys, names UPMC Presenting Sponsor of Panther Women's Sports, and brings UPMC signage to new Victory Heights Arena & Sports Performance Center.

PITTSBURGH
- Pitt Athletics and its multimedia rights holder JMI Sports, today announced a multiyear expansion of its longstanding partnership with UPMC to include three core components: a UPMC patch on Pitt Football jerseys, Presenting Sponsor status of Panther Women's Sports - to include a comprehensive women's health platform - and premium signage opportunities at the new Victory Heights Sports Performance Center and Arena, which opened earlier this month.

The UPMC jersey patch for Pitt Football marks the first agreement of its kind announced at Pitt and will debut at the season opener on Saturday, September 5 vs. Miami (Ohio) at Pitt's own Acrisure Stadium.

"UPMC is one of the most respected names in health care, with a global impact on medicine, research and patient care," Pitt Director of Athletics
C. Allen Greene
said. "They're a pillar in our community and there's not a brand more ingrained with Pitt Athletics. That made them a natural choice for our first jersey patch partner. This partnership goes well beyond a transaction. It reflects two institutions equally committed to the health and success of our region. We're equally excited about UPMC becoming the presenting sponsor of women's sports. It gives our student-athletes a unique platform to work alongside UPMC's physicians and health care providers in promoting women's health and wellness across our region."

The expanded agreement builds on a longstanding relationship between Pitt Athletics and UPMC, which has served as the University's Official Health Care Provider and a Lead Partner across Pitt Athletics since 1986, when the late Dr. Freddie Fu founded Pitt's renowned sports medicine program.

The expansion continues to strengthen the pillars on which the partnership was founded by also becoming the Presenting Sponsor of Panther Women's Sports, which will include the creation of an interactive platform for promoting women's health through community educational programs and activities such as health screenings, fairs and awareness campaigns that will feature Pitt women student-athletes as role models and influencers.

"We are thrilled with this opportunity to continue supporting the health and well-being of Pitt student-athletes and the halo effect it has on our greater community," said MaCalus Hogan, MD, MBA, chair, Department of Orthopaedic Surgery at Pitt and UPMC Sports Medicine. "The exciting and unique partnership between Pitt women student-athletes and UPMC women's health experts will allow us to combine the athlete experience and storytelling with a focus on important health initiatives and programming that we hope will positively impact women across our region." Beyond sports medicine, topics will include women's heart health, mental health, diseases prevention and more.

JMI Sports – operating locally as Pitt Sports Marketing – worked in collaboration with Pitt Athletics on the expansion of this agreement with UPMC, with the goal of elevating the partnership framework to include new multimedia assets that reflect the industry-leading innovation taking place across the athletic department. As such, the expanded partnership includes UPMC branding inside the new Victory Heights Arena and its Sports Performance Center, both of which opened August 13.

"UPMC is already woven into the fabric of Pitt, which makes this next chapter of our partnership especially important," said Paul Archey, President at JMI Sports. "Having a Pittsburgh-based company featured across assets of this scale and visibility is a powerful reflection of a best-in-class partner, with an organic connection to the program and university. We are excited by their ambition to grow alongside us and take advantage of new partnership opportunities as the industry changes."

ABOUT PITT ATHLETICS

The University of Pittsburgh Department of Athletics sponsors 19 varsity sports and is a proud member of the Atlantic Coast Conference. Committed to excellence in competition, academics and community, Pitt Athletics develops student-athletes who compete at the highest level while preparing them for success beyond sport. For more information, visit
pittsburghpanthers.com
.

ABOUT JMI SPORTS

JMI Sports
is a leading media rights and venue development company that provides management of collegiate multimedia rights, sponsorship sales agency representation, and project management expertise for the development of collegiate and professional sports facilities. The company serves to maximize each client's economic potential through customized initiatives, from marketing and branding solutions to facility design strategies.

JMI Sports' signature collegiate multimedia rights partnerships include the University of Kentucky, UCLA, the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Pittsburgh, Harvard University, Columbia University, San Diego State University, University of California at San Diego, University of San Diego, and joint-venture properties at the University of Georgia (with Learfield) and University of Notre Dame (with Legends). JMI Sports also represents multimedia rights for several conferences, including the Ivy League, the Mid-American Conference, the Mountain West Conference, the Patriot League, and the Atlantic 10, and serves as third-party sales representation for premier sports properties, venues, and events including Rupp Arena at Central Bank Center, the Rose Bowl, the Penn Relays, and USA Volleyball.

JMI Sports was founded in 2006 by CEO Erik Judson and technology entrepreneur John Moores, former owner of the San Diego Padres. To learn more, please visit
www.jmisports.com
.

ABOUT UPMC

UPMC is a world-renowned, non-profit health care provider and insurer committed to delivering exceptional, people-centered care and community services. Headquartered in Pittsburgh and affiliated with the University of Pittsburgh Schools of the Health Sciences, UPMC is shaping the future of health through clinical and technological innovation, research, and education. Dedicated to advancing the well-being of our diverse communities, we provide $2 billion annually in community benefits, more than any other health system in Pennsylvania. Our 100,000 employees - including more than 5,000 physicians - care for patients across more than 40 hospitals and 800 outpatient sites in Pennsylvania, New York and Maryland, as well as overseas.  UPMC Insurance Services covers more than 4 million members, providing affordable, high-quality value-based care.  To learn more, visit
UPMC.com
.

; new video series, written features and Director of Storytelling
Abby Schnable
headline expansive platform built for today's fan

PITTSBURGH –
Pitt fans are about to get more access than ever before. Pitt Athletics today launched new storytelling and multimedia content initiatives designed to take fans inside the programs, the people and the moments that define what it means to be a Panther, at a moment when authentic fan connection matters more than ever in college athletics.

The platform spans audio, video and written content, each pillar built around a simple idea: fans deserve more than highlights and headlines. They deserve the full story.

A STORYTELLER AT THE CENTER

Leading the initiative is
Abby Schnable
, who joins Pitt Athletics as Director of Storytelling & Multimedia Content. Schnable spent years covering Pitt Athletics at the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, reporting across football, men's and women's basketball, volleyball and Olympic sports – sitting in coaches' offices, following student-athletes through their journeys and finding the stories that live beneath the surface of the box score.

Now she'll be telling those stories from the inside.

Schnable will oversee the department's long-form and multimedia storytelling initiatives, leading written features and driving content across PittsburghPanthers.com and social platforms. She also serves as Executive Producer of "Beyond the Script," the flagship podcast of the new initiative.

Schnable introduces herself and the initiative in her own words. Read her opening column here.

BEYOND THE SCRIPT PODCAST

The flagship of the new initiative, "Beyond the Script" is a long-form audio series hosted by
Jason Earle
that takes listeners inside Pitt Athletics with coaches, student-athletes, staff and the people shaping the direction of the program. The podcast debuts Tuesday, July 7, with Athletic Director
Allen Greene
as the inaugural guest, and will be available across all major streaming platforms.

VIDEO SERIES

A suite of rotating weekly video series gives fans immersive, in-depth access to the people and programs of Pitt Athletics. Each series is built to tell a distinct dimension of the student-athlete experience:

Panther Tales
– Long-form storytelling that connects student-athletes to the full value of a Pitt education, spotlighting the academic achievements, athletic pursuits and community engagement made possible through Panther Club scholarship support.

Panthers All Access
– An inside look at Pitt Athletics in competition, training and preparation, capturing the intensity and culture of the programs behind the scenes.

Pitt Paths
– A behind-the-scenes look at student-athlete life off the field and outside the arena, highlighting academic development, career preparation and the Pitt experience beyond competition.

Roc's Rewind
– A film-focused segment in which a student-athlete or coach breaks down a defining play, moment or game, offering fans a rare look inside the strategic and emotional dimensions of competition.

WRITTEN FEATURES

The initiative's written features operation publishes across PittsburghPanthers.com and social platforms, anchored by weekly sport features that go beyond the scoreboard, while offering fans behind-the-scenes access and in-depth storytelling from inside Pitt's programs throughout the year. A Sunday Sidebar column provides a consistent weekly editorial presence across the athletics department.

SPORT-SPECIFIC NIL CONTENT

The initiative also includes dedicated sport-specific, NIL-focused content series creating branded storytelling opportunities that benefit student-athletes while extending the reach and relevance of Pitt Athletics content across key audience segments.

A PLATFORM FOR PARTNERS

The initiative creates a robust inventory of sponsorship and partnership opportunities for brands seeking meaningful connection with Pitt Athletics fans and the broader Pittsburgh market. From podcast integrations to video series presenting sponsorships, the platform is built with commercial partnership in mind – offering partners premium placement within high-quality, audience-first content.

For more information on Pitt Athletics, visit pittsburghpanthers.com or follow @Pitt_ATHLETICS on social media.

SPRINGFIELD, Mass.  –
Pitt women's basketball senior guard
Taryn Barbot
has been named to the 2027 Ann Meyers Drysdale Award Watch List, the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame announced Tuesday.

The Ann Meyers Drysdale Award, presented in partnership with the Women's Basketball Coaches Association (WBCA), honors the top shooting guard in NCAA Division I women's college basketball. The award is named after Naismith Basketball Hall of Famer Ann Meyers Drysdale, the first player, regardless of gender, to be selected to an All-America Team in four consecutive college seasons.

Barbot is one of 20 players nationally named to the 2027 watch list. The Floral Park, N.Y., native enters her senior season at Pitt following a standout three-year career at College of Charleston, where she established herself as one of the nation's premier scoring guards.

In 2025-26, Barbot earned CAA Player of the Year, All-CAA First Team, CAA All-Defensive Team and CAA Tournament Most Outstanding Player honors after leading the Cougars to a historic season. She started all 33 games and averaged 20.1 points per game, ranking 16th nationally in scoring while leading the CAA in scoring, 3-point field goals per game (2.5), 3-point field-goal percentage (36.1) and free-throw percentage (87.2).

Barbot scored 664 points during the 2025-26 season, setting Charleston's Division I single-season scoring record, while becoming the program's all-time Division I scoring leader with 1,715 career points. She also recorded 82 3-pointers, 109 assists and 77 steals on the season.

The senior guard posted four 30-point performances in 2025-26, including a 36-point effort in the first round of the NCAA Tournament at No. 3 Duke. Her 36 points marked the most scored by an individual player in an NCAA Tournament game at Cameron Indoor Stadium.

The 20-player Ann Meyers Drysdale Award Watch List will be narrowed to 10 candidates in February before being trimmed to five finalists in March. Players can play their way onto and off the list at any point during the 2026-27 season.

COUGAR BASKETBALL CAMP

07/27/2026 - 07/31/2026   M - F, 9:00 AM - 3:00 PM
AFC, AFC Pool
Ages 4-14 | Grades Pre-K to 8th
The Chatham Cougar Basketball Camp philosophy and goals are to help youth basketball players learn the game of basketball in a fun-filled environment. Our camp is designed to teach the fundamentals and skills of the game of basketball while promoting teamwork, leadership and good sportsmanship. Many of our sessions will involve 1 player -1 ball to maximize repetitions and keep children engaged. Each day will consist of new technical training followed by fun games where your child can practice their newfound skills! We welcome all levels of skill and campers will be divided into groups based on age and ability.
Camper drop-off is between 8:30 and 9:00 AM and pickup is between 3:00 and 3:15 PM.
Swim time may be offered but is not guaranteed based on facilities and availability

COUGARS SOCCER CAMP

08/03/2026 - 08/07/2026   M - F, 9:00 AM - 3:00 PM
Field, AFC, AFC Pool
Ages 4-14 | Grades Pre-K to 8th
The Chatham Cougar Soccer Camp philosophy and goals are to help youth soccer players learn the game of soccer in a fun-filled environment. Our camp is designed to teach the fundamentals and skills of the game of soccer while promoting teamwork, leadership and good sportsmanship. Many of our sessions will involve 1 player -1 ball to maximize touches and keep children engaged. Each day will consist of new technical training followed by fun games where your child can practice their new found skills! We welcome all levels of skill and campers will be divided into groups based on age and ability.
Camper drop-off is between 8:30 and 9:00 AM and pickup is between 3:00 and 3:15 PM.
Swim time may be offered but is not guaranteed based on facilities and availability.
Daily lunch is included in the registration fee and every camper will receive a camp shirt.

LACROSSE

Chatham Men's Lacrosse Youth Boy's Camp
07/06/2026 - 07/09/2026 M-Th, 9 AM - 3 PM
AFC Pool, Classroom, Field/Gym
Boys
The premier Youth Lacrosse instructional summer camp in the Pittsburgh area held on the beautiful and historic Shadyside campus of Chatham University. This is a great opportunity to develop and refine your skills with high level instruction from college coaches and players.  Our goal is to create an environment of learning, fun, and growth for the love of the game that allows for improved skills to emerge for every camper.  Don't miss out on a chance to elevate your game!  Areas of focus will be:
1 on 1 player development with positional focus.
Team concepts for improved lacrosse IQ.
Small sided games and Skills competitions.
Athletic training development conducive to the game of Lacrosse.
Offensive and Defensive competitive gameplay.
Necessary equipment:
Stick / Helmet / Gloves / Arm Pads / Shoulder Pads / Cleats and Shoes / Mouth Piece / Water Bottle / Throat and Chest protector for Goalies.
Camper drop-off is between 8:30 and 9:00 AM and pickup is between 3:00 and 3:15 PM. (12:00 PM - 12:15 PM pickup for Half Day campers)
Swim time may be offered but is not guaranteed based on facilities and availability.

SWIMMING

08/13/2026 - 08/16/2026   M - F, 9:00 AM - 3:00 PM
9:00AM-11:30AM (12-18) ; 12:30PM-3:00PM (11 and Under)
AFC, AFC Pool
Ages 5-11 (in the afternoon) 12-18 (in the morning)
Dive into three exciting days of learning, movement, and fun at our 3-Day Cougars Swim Clinic, designed for swimmers ages 5–18 (must still be in high school) of all skill levels—from beginners building confidence in the water to competitive swimmers refining race skills. Campers must be able to complete at least a 25 of each stroke, and a 50 free without assistance or stopping. 12 and Over Campers will attend the morning session while 11 and Under campers will attend the afternoon session
Each day will feature age- and ability-based groupings to ensure swimmers receive instruction that is safe, engaging, and developmentally appropriate. Campers will work with experienced, passionate Chatham Coaches and Student Athletes in a positive and encouraging environment that emphasizes both skill development and a love for the sport.
What Swimmers Will Learn:
Stroke fundamentals & refinement for all four competitive strokes
Starts, turns, and finishes
Body position, balance, and efficient technique
Age-appropriate endurance, speed, and skill work
Race skills and confidence-building
Camp Highlights:
Small group instruction with individualized feedback
Daily in-water skill progressions and drills
Fun games, relays, and friendly competitions
Focus on safety, sportsmanship, and teamwork
High-energy, supportive atmosphere for all swimmers

Whether your child is new to the pool or looking to take their swimming to the next level, this 3-Day Swim Clinic is a great opportunity to learn, grow, and have fun in the water. Swimmers should bring a suit, cap, goggles, towel, water bottle, their equipment bag, and a great attitude!
12 and Over Camper drop off 8:30am-9:00am, Camper Pick Up 11:30am-11:45am
11 and Under Camper drop off 12:00pm-12:30pm, Camper Pick up 3:00pm-3:15pm
Come swim, learn, and make a splash with us!
Camper drop-off is 8:30AM-9:00AM and pick up is 11:30-11:45, 12:00PM-12:30PM and pickup is 3:00PM-3:15PM.

SOFTBALL PROSPECT CAMP

08/29/2026
9:00AM-3:00 PM
West Field
Grades 9-12
If you feel you have what it takes to play at the next level, then come to our softball prospect camp and match your skills against other highly talented players. Show our coaching staff your A game.
The morning session will consist of defensive drills and front toss, Conducted by Chatham softball coaching staff and current Chatham players.
The afternoon session will be live games.
Highlights:
There will be a question and answer session with current Chatham softball players.
A campus tour will be offered at the conclusion of the camp.

m.marsili@chatham.edu

Center for American Music

About the Library
The Center for American Music, a part of the University of Pittsburgh Library System,  engages in research, teaching, interpretive presentations, and conservation of music of the United States of America. We expand and document knowledge of American music, as well as its cultural and social roles in American life.
Our Foster Hall Collection reflects a broad cross-section of American popular culture, especially from the 1840s to the 1930s. In addition to containing one of the most significant collections of 19th-century American music, we are also the principal repository for materials concerning the life and music of
Stephen Collins Foster
, a Pittsburgh native who was America's first professional songwriter.
The Center for American Music is housed in the Stephen Foster Memorial building alongside the Stephen Foster Memorial Museum and two theatres.
Voices Across Time
, the Center's education project, is creating tools for middle and high school social studies and language arts teachers to use music every day in their classrooms.

General Collection Development Policy: Collections Maintenance

Collection management is a series of activities that guides the stewardship of our general print and physical media collections. These procedures ensure that physical collections in our libraries are meeting the evolving needs of our patrons, that we maintain enough space to add new materials, that our on-site collections are optimized for use, that fragile and/or valuable materials are protected, and all materials are well cared for. It comprises a set of regular tasks that are necessary to keep the library's materials organized, ensuring efficient access for both internal and external users. These tasks apply to all ULS general collections, across all ULS locations.

Library collections will be transferred to storage to:

Maintain adequate shelf capacity to allow for growth and shifting across entire collection, and within LC classes.

Ensure enhanced security for rare or valuable materials.

Meet preservation needs of individual items.

Materials considered for storage transfer will be identified using the following general criteria:

Physical condition of the item (
see damaged materials policy and workflow document
). (
restricted access
)

Need for additional security, for rare or valuable items.

Publication and/or acquisition date.

Total circulation count and most recent circulation date.

Availability of space (based on the previous year’s growth and physical inspection of shelving).

Other local conditions and considerations.

If an identical item is already available at another ULS location, it will not be eligible for transfer and should be considered for re-housing.

Generally, a transfer of physical collections to offsite storage facility will take place annually. Individual items, e.g., damaged or requiring additional protection, can be transferred at any time. Any routine requests for transfer can be suspended if larger or urgent transfer projects emerge.

Associated documentation:
(restricted access)

Transferring General Collections to LCSU.

Transferring Rare Books to LCSU.

In some cases, materials can be restored from off-site storage to locations on campus. These can happen when:

Materials are frequently requested (based on usage reports).

Materials are needed to support a new class or program.

Materials are needed for use at short notice.

All deaccessioning decisions must balance the needs of our community, the sharing agreements with our partners, and space and other considerations that the ULS may have. De-accessioning may take place when there is:

Redundancy:

Multiple copies of the same item,

Duplication between physical and (perpetual access) digital collections, or between the ULS holdings and those of organizations where we have reciprocal borrowing agreements, if any.

Poor physical condition:

Damage that cannot be repaired without expensive and time-intensive conservation treatments or cannot be repaired, e.g., mold, vandalism that renders the content unusable, and

Large sections of missing pages.

Certain outdated or inaccurate content (as exemplified by older textbook editions that are no longer considered accurate by a consensus in the field), unless the material contributes to a research collection.

Materials whose format, ephemeral nature, or primary purpose renders them of decreasing value to a research collection over time, such as curriculum kits, teaching aids, items with obsolete or deteriorating non-print components, or similar instructional and practice-based materials not intended for long-term research use.

In exceptional circumstances, by request:
see Returning or Withdrawing General Collections Materials policy.

Damaged Materials

Damaged materials from the general collections that are defined as those that cannot be easily mended by access services staff are transferred to LCSU for additional assessment and disposition. Each item is reviewed for duplication at ULS, total and recent circulation activity, any retention obligations, and overall physical condition. Depending on the factors described above, an item can be:

Ingested to LCSU with a note about the extent of damage.

Replaced by a new copy and de-accessioned.

De-accessioned.

Note: in certain circumstances, material may be sent for conservation.

Lost and Missing Materials

Lost items are identified as on loan and not returned within 28 days of the loan expiry date.

Missing items are those not found in stacks following three searches conducted within the first 48 hours of patron request and are not on loan.

Lists of missing and lost items are generated monthly for replacement decisions. In general,./p>

Items from “popular” collections (e.g. Alldred) are not replaced.

Items for which there is another ULS copy are not replaced.

Other criteria for replacement decision include: age, recent usage, availability of newer editions, etc.

General Collections Development Policy: An Overview

This policy sets out the criteria for management of the ULS general collections. It provides guidance on our approach to acquisitions and collections maintenance, and relations with other libraries. Links are provided to associated procedures. We acknowledge that an increasing amount of highly relevant scholarly content exists outside library collections (e.g., open access journals, government policy documents, company information); such materials are outside the scope of this policy. Our liaison librarians and functional specialists can provide expertise with locating, accessing, and evaluating such information.

To meet the information needs of our communities, we understand the scope of this policy to include materials owned or licensed; shared collections; and collective collections. We will continuously monitor the balance between these three categories. The shift to increasingly electronic collections has created an environment in which information provision is no longer confined to local holdings. Through conscious coordination, we increase overall collection breadth and depth through sustainable investment in collections, and regional and national collaborations to build, share, and preserve collective collections. For instance, we participate in several consortia that support purchasing, collaborative or shared collection development (EAST and Hathi Trust, CRL) and enable resource sharing (e.g., PALCI EZBorrow, OCLC Interlibrary Loan, or RapidILL).

Our priorities for the collection development are three-fold:

align with the current and future research and teaching needs of the University,

complement our special and archival collections, and

build on areas of collection strengths.

University of Pittsburgh Library System

Theodore M. Finney Music Library

Welcome!
Located in the basement of the Music Building, the Finney Music Library supports the learning and research needs of the Music Department (graduate programs in composition and theory, ethnomusicology, jazz studies, and musicology, and the undergraduate program), the University’s Oakland campus, and the wider local, regional, and international music communities.
The Finney Music Library is much more than just a collection of music resources. We’re a laboratory for independent exploration and high technology scholarship. We offer sophisticated playback equipment for CDs, LPs, DVDs, and VHS tapes, public computers, and quiet and comfortable places to study. We also have a dedicated collaborative workspace, with video monitor and playback equipment for your group to study. Our highly trained and dedicated library staff organizes and assists with the collections, equipment, and networked technology. We also provide formal instruction in the use of our resources.
All of our available collections are in open stacks and include books, journals, and music scores. Miniature scores, oversized, and folio scores are housed separately. Rich holdings in Western art music, world music, and popular music of all kinds make our library a one-stop-shop for music study. Our distinguished reference collection contains music dictionaries, encyclopedias, bibliographies, and collected works editions of composers from J. S. Bach to Shostakovich, and everything in-between.
Sound and video recordings are housed in closed stacks behind our Circulation Desk. This area also houses the John Coltrane tenor solos collection and a collection of jazz fake books. Our rare collections include important music imprints and manuscripts from 15th to the 19th centuries, and an impressive collection of facsimiles of composer manuscripts of all periods. If you need help finding materials or assistance with your research, ask us at the Circulation and Reference desks.
Coupled with the impressive collections in all of Pitt’s campus and regional libraries, the Finney Music Library stands as one of the most important music research centers in the United States.

Reload via ULS
If you often come across online article citations, but cannot view the full text because you are not logged in remotely to the ULS Web site, then set up "Reload via ULS" on your computer or mobile device.
"Reload via ULS" provides instant access to full-text articles that are available through ULS subscriptions.
For desktop and laptop computers:
Drag the dark blue "Reload via ULS" bookmarklet to your Web browser's bookmarks toolbar.
When viewing an article citation, click on the bookmarklet in your toolbar.
The EZproxy login box will appear. Enter your login information to have access to the full text if ULS has a subscription to the article.

Go to Google Scholar’s Settings > Library Links
Search for University of Pittsburgh
Select “University of Pittsburgh – Full-Text@Pitt” and save your settings
Conduct your search in Google Scholar
Once you find a suitable resource click on the link for “Full-Text @ Pitt” on the right side of the resource title. You will then be prompted to enter your Pitt username and password for access to resource

University of Pittsburgh Library System

Russian, East European & Eurasian Studies Collection

The term
Russian, East European & Eurasian Studies
at the University of Pittsburgh refers to material from and about the following countries:

Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia-Hercegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Estonia, Georgia, Hungary, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Poland, Romania, Russia, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, and Uzbekistan.

This interdisciplinary subject area covers nearly all areas of the social sciences and humanities related to these countries, as well as material on their environments. The material is in English, the languages of these countries, and other Western languages.

Hillman Library Resources

The Russian, East European & Eurasian collection consists of over 600,000 volumes, of which a very substantial number are in the languages of the area, plus hundreds of newspapers and periodicals from or about the region. Many of the latter are in electronic format, on external databases, or on CD-ROM. The East European collection includes nearly 100,000 holdings in Polish literature, history, politics, and culture as well as rare books, newspapers, and musical scores that were formerly housed at Alliance College.

Strengths of the collection are Russian and Polish history, literature, culture, political science, economics, international relations, and the life of immigrants from these REEES countries in the United States. Polish-American resources are especially well-represented at the University of Pittsburgh. There is also a special collection of Slovak monographs and serials. Pitt has been actively working to enhance the Slovak, Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, and Romanian collections overall. An extensive exchange program of materials with Russian and East European institutions provides material unavailable through other sources.

Holdings estimates are currently about 56 percent Russian-centered, 18 percent Polish, 9 percent Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, 9 percent Romanian, and 8 percent Slovak.

Video Collection

A collection of over 8,000 Russian, East European & Eurasian films, which is under continuous development, is housed in the University's
Stark Media Resource Center
located in Hillman Library.

Other Library Collections

Other materials relating to the region are found in the
Frick Fine Arts Library
, and the libraries of the
Barco Law School
and
Katz Graduate School of Business
.

.

Theatrical and musical performance are among the few mediums in which transgender, gender-nonconforming, and crossdressing individuals find acceptance, community, and vocational roles in an otherwise hostile society. This collection provides a modest introduction to the rich diversity and historical significance of these communities.

Gender-nonconforming individuals have often held roles performing religious music and rituals. One of the earliest such historical attestations depicts gender-nonconforming priestesses to the goddess Inanna in ancient Mesopotamia, as described in Inanna: Lady of Largest Heart.

Crossdressing in performance has regularly been used as a response to gender restricting laws in theatre. For example, in Classical Greece, Elizabethan England, and Edo Japan, women were banned from performing on stage, compelling male actors to play female roles. Conversely, European opera often featured women performing ‘trouser roles’ – portrayals of youthful men – after the decline in popularity and eventual banning of castrati.

In more recent years, crossdressing, transgender, and gender-nonconforming performers have gained wider acceptance in the United States, reflected in the popularity of live and televised drag shows, whose contemporary origins lie in the Harlem drag balls vividly depicted in the groundbreaking documentary Paris is Burning.

The University of Pittsburgh Library System is unique in that it holds two archival collections directly related to this subject: the Mildred Miller Posvar Papers, which document the life of the longtime mezzo-soprano at the Metropolitan Opera, who was iconic for her trouser roles; and Kōgyo: The Art of Noh, which features woodblock prints depicting male Noh actors portraying male and female characters.

This collection also includes literature on contemporary transgender, gender-nonconforming, and crossdressing performers in communities across the globe, and the use of makeup, costuming, mannerisms, and singing techniques to depict gender on stage.

The Women in International Education Collection is dedicated to exploring the roles, contributions, and experiences of women within global education systems and international academic environments. This spotlight collection spans multiple disciplines, including education, sociology, gender studies, international relations, and global development, providing a multifaceted view of the intersection between gender and education across diverse cultural, geopolitical, and historical contexts. Key areas of focus within the collection include:

Historical and Contemporary Perspectives: Materials examine the historical development of women’s involvement in education worldwide, tracing key milestones such as women’s access to higher education, the rise of female educators, and the evolution of policies promoting gender equity in educational systems.

Global Educational Policies and Gender Equality: The collection includes resources on international frameworks, such as UNESCO’s initiatives on gender parity in education, as well as regional and national policies that aim to empower women through educational access and leadership opportunities.

Women as Educators and Leaders: The collection features works on the role of women as teachers, administrators, and scholars in international contexts. It also highlights the experiences of women in leadership positions in global education organizations, examining the barriers they face and the strategies they employ to advocate for change.

Gender and Educational Access: A significant portion of the collection focuses on gender-based disparities in educational access, particularly in developing countries, and the ways in which women’s education is impacted by social, economic, political, and cultural factors.

Intersectionality and Education: Recognizing the complexity of women’s identities, the collection explores intersectionality in global education, addressing how race, class, ethnicity, religion, and other factors intersect with gender to influence educational experiences and outcomes for women.

Scholarship and Feminist Theories in Education: Scholarly works on feminist pedagogies, critical gender theory, and postcolonial critiques of education are integral to the collection, providing theoretical frameworks for understanding women’s roles in shaping and being shaped by educational systems around the world.

Through its diverse range of materials, the collection fosters a deeper understanding of how women contribute to and are impacted by the global educational landscape, while supporting the ongoing work of promoting gender equity in education worldwide.

The horror genre is one of most enduring forms of storytelling both in literature and film. It thrives on its ability to entertain, thrill, repulse, and terrify readers and viewers. It also offers a framework for understanding and exploring our fears, both personal and societal. Horror explores these fears through a broad spectrum of approaches that includes both realism and the supernatural: from quiet psychological thrillers to rampaging monsters; from haunted houses to body horror; from historical periods to speculative futures; and from extreme gore to goofy comedy. It is a rich genre, diverse in both its themes and content as well as its creators. This spotlight collection features a variety of titles across the genre to serve as both an entry point for newcomers and somewhere to find something new for dedicated fans. It features classic works in film and literature; winners of the major horror literary awards, the Bram Stoker and Shirley Jackson Awards; and works from authors whose papers can be found in the horror studies collection in Archives & Special Collections.

This year’s spotlight collection explores the themes of race, gender, and identity, highlighting the diverse experiences and narratives within the Asian American community. By fostering understanding and solidarity among marginalized voices, the collection draws from the Pitt University of Pittsburgh Library System’s extensive Asian American literature collections, and features around thirty 30 carefully selected titles.

This showcase exemplifies contemporary Asian American authors who advocate for their communities from the National Medal awardee Maxine Hong Kingston, whose seminal works like The Woman Warrior and China Men examine the complexities of identity and gender within the Asian American experience, to Pulitzer Prize finalist Cathy Park Hong, whose powerful essays in Minor Feelings: An Asian American Reckoning delve into the emotional and societal struggles faced by Asian American women, this showcase exemplifies contemporary Asian American authors who advocate for their communities. Kingston’s narrative style weaves together personal and collective histories, while Hong’s incisive critique addresses the intersections of race, gender, and culture.

For those interested in Asian American racial identity and social realities, the 2020 book Envisioning Religion, Race, and Asian Americans explores the complex intersections of religion and racial identity among Asian American communities, highlighting how these dynamics shape cultural experiences. Through this diverse array of perspectives, the collection emphasizes the importance of intersectionality in addressing the unique challenges faced by Asian Americans and advocates for a more inclusive dialogue on identity and social justice.

We are collaborating with the Alliance of Queer and Underrepresented Asians in Recognition of Intersectionality to Uphold Solidarity (AQUARIUS) and the Asian Students Alliance (ASA) to host events that promote awareness for API Month.

In the preface to their historical and critical account of transness in cinema, Corpses, Fools and Monsters: The History and Future of Transness in Cinema, Willow Maclay and Caden Gardner write:

“I don’t think movies are the be-all, end-all for social change or anything of the sort, but there’s certainly something symptomatic in the American psyche where for the most part the only times we’ve been on screen are to be murdered, turned into a joke, or a tragedy of failed transition. The mainstream isn’t interested in our livelihood or our goals. It’s a lost highway of corpses, fools and monsters.”

The authors go on to describe the presence of trans subjects in the history of cinema, the role trans artists and advocates have played in reclaiming and reconstituting that history, and what future there may be for trans filmmakers, performers, artists, and authors.

This spotlight collection uses their account as a point of departure for exploring the presence of trans artists in this medium and others. Because it encapsulates only what is in one library’s collection, and trans art and artists remain underrepresented in this collection and many others, we encourage users to seek work beyond the scope of this collection—and let us know what voices and works YOU think should be represented in this collection in the future!

This Spotlight Collection honors two pioneering queens of mystery—Agatha Christie and Mary Roberts Rinehart—whose extraordinary lives rivaled the intrigue of their fiction. 2026 is the 150th anniversary of Mary Roberts Rinehart’s birth and the 50th anniversary of Agatha Christie’s death. Both women revolutionized detective literature and influenced generations of suspense writers. Christie created the legendary Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple, while Rinehart pioneered the "Had I But Known" narrative style which compares the character’s foolish actions to what they might have done had they known all the facts.

Beyond their literary achievements, these remarkable authors led adventurous lives that defied the constraints of their era.  Christie accompanied her archaeologist husband on digs across the Middle East.  Rinehart, equally intrepid, worked as a war correspondent during World War I, becoming one of the first journalists to reach the Belgian front lines and interviewing Queen Mary of England as well as other notable figures.

Both women witnessed the tumult of two world wars, experiences that profoundly shaped their writing. Rinehart served as a nurse and reported from European battlefields, while Christie worked in hospital dispensaries, gaining the pharmaceutical knowledge that made her poison plots devastatingly authentic. Their combined works showcase not only masterful plotting and unforgettable characters but also the indomitable spirit of two women who lived as boldly as they wrote.

This collection features a mix of nonfiction and fiction books, films, and online resources that highlight the experiences of diverse disability communities. Topics include blindness, deafness, neurodiversity, and mobility disabilities.

Showcasing collections like this helps increase disability representation and awareness. Representation matters, as it provides characters and narratives that members of the disability community can connect with and helps affirm that they are not alone in their experiences. Materials included in this collection also offer opportunities to share these perspectives with a broader audience. By highlighting these stories, the collection aims to foster greater awareness, understanding, and acceptance among the able-bodied community and beyond.

The University Library System has strong collections pertaining to jazz. Although many materials can be found in the Theodore M. The University Library System has over 40,000 records, CDs, and other physical recording formats, many of which are unavailable to stream online. You can find them in PittCat and listen to them at home or in Finney Music Library.

A much-beloved writer, the works of Jane Austen are funny, romantic, and sharply satirical. Whether you’ve been an Austen fan for decades, or the latest Pride and Prejudice adaptation has recently caught your eye, we welcome you to peruse this Spotlight Collection.

This collection contains all of Austen’s major novels (Sense and Sensibility, Pride and Prejudice, Mansfield Park, Emma, Northanger Abbey, and Persuasion), as well as her unfinished works and early unpublished writings. You will also find an array of filmed adaptations, from straightforward renditions of her novels to modernized interpretations.

Looking to delve deeper into Austen scholarship? This collection showcases numerous critical responses to Austen’s work, examining her novels from a variety of engaging scholarly lenses.

In our busy, oversaturated lives, it’s common to rapidly consume one piece of media after another. By examining the oeuvre and critical reception of a sole author, this collection encourages readers to slow down and experience Austen’s works thoughtfully and comprehensively, fostering a deeper understanding of her life, her work, and the society that she was so fond of satirizing.

The very best adaptation/expansion, reimagining mines an already established and valued narrative for deeper meaning and fresh insight. Humans are born storytellers. Whether from oral tradition, written word, or created through other media, a tale impacts culture at a specific time and with a particular audience. Some tales, though, persist over time and are shared again and again. In some cases, the narrative barely alters. But sometimes, a retelling/retooling bursts through, imbued with transformative changes that engage, delight, and challenge. This Spotlight offers the opportunity to enjoy a great story. As you read or listen, perhaps consider why some stories are revisited. What has changed? Why? Who has made the change?

These materials highlight creators referencing known works in surprising ways, captivating audiences anew, possibly employing modern technologies or alternative formats. There are retellings once directed at adult audiences now targeted at youth, and younger fare fashioned for mature audiences. Some reimaginings flip the narrative in terms of elements such as gender, class, locale, age, genre, or time period. You’ll find a heady mix of scary, delightful, disturbing, and nostalgic within this assortment. We invite you to explore these stories—traditional and newly-wrought—that continue to engage and shape popular culture.

Red horses frolicking in a yellow field, a great white shark in a tank of formaldehyde, white peacocks peacefully preening, a rhinoceros named Clara, these are a few of the participants in our animal parade.

This selection from the Frick Fine Arts Library Collection reflects the evolving role of animals in the human imagination and the visual arts. Poetic, realistic, dreamlike or ominous, these powerful images invite us to contemplate the everlasting fascination of artists for the animal kingdom. Comprised of art books and graphic novels, it addresses themes as varied as anthropomorphism, rituals, symbolism, ecological crisis, and posthumanism. It is also a rich interdisciplinary source of inspiration for students, researchers, art lovers, animal enthusiasts and inquiring minds alike.

The Ethnic Studies Spotlight collection is a collaborative initiative between the East Asian Library and the Center for Ethnic Studies Research (CESR), designed to highlight and support underrepresented areas within Ethnic Studies. The collection focuses on key communities central to the field—including Asian American, Black, Indigenous / Aboriginal and Pasifika, Latine groups—approached through local, regional, comparative, and transnational lenses. By curating works that explore the experiences and contributions of these communities, the collection aims to enrich scholarly resources, raise awareness of lesser-known narratives, and encourage deeper engagement with the diverse dimensions of race and ethnicity in the United States and beyond.

In a world increasingly shaped by digital connectivity, the year 2025 stands as a critical juncture for cybersecurity. From personal data on our smartphones to the complex networks that run our global infrastructure, every aspect of modern life is intertwined with technology. This dependence, however, brings with it a new set of risks. Cyber threats are a daily reality, with attacks becoming more sophisticated, automated, and powered by the same artificial intelligence that promises to make our lives easier. This book display explores the multifaceted landscape of cybersecurity today, offering a curated selection of resources that illuminate the challenges and solutions of this ever-evolving field.

As students and members of a university community, understanding cybersecurity is more than just a matter of technical knowledge—it’s about digital citizenship. Whether you’re a computer science major, a budding journalist, or a history student, the principles of protecting information and navigating the digital world securely are relevant to your academic and personal life. This collection delves into topics ranging from the evolution of ransomware and supply chain attacks to the critical role of biometric authentication and the looming threat of quantum computing. We invite you to explore these works and gain a deeper appreciation for the complex interplay of technology, privacy, and security in the 21st century.

Meyer’s Konversations-Lexikon, published by the Bibliographisches Institut founded by Joseph Meyer in 1826, was one of the leading German-language encyclopedias throughout the 19th and 20th centuries. Following Germany’s division after the Second World War and the foundation of two ideologically competing German states in 1949 – the Federal Republic of Germany, a western-style parliamentary democracy, and the German Democratic Republic (GDR), a Soviet-style socialist nation controlled by its communist party –, Meyer’s encyclopedia took a dramatic turn. From then on, it was published in two ideologically distinct versions. One was published by the now state-owned VEB Bibliographisches Institut in Leipzig, GDR, and the other by the Bibliographisches Institut in Mannheim, Federal Republic of Germany, established there by its former owners in 1953.

To mark the 150th anniversary of the Bibliographisches Institut in 1976, the two publishing houses produced ambitious and competing new editions of their encyclopedias: Meyer’s Neues Lexikon (18 vols., Leipzig, 1971-1978) and Meyer’s Enzyklopädisches Lexikon (25 vols., Mannheim, 1971-1979). Each represents a milestone in the history of encyclopedia publishing. The East German version was the last one ever produced in the GDR; the West German one saw one more edition before the Bibliographisches Institut in 1984 merged with F. A. Brockhaus, the other famous publisher of German-language encyclopedias.

Encyclopedias claim to present the knowledge of their time in an unbiased manner. However, a comparison of Meyer’s Neues Lexikon and Meyer’s Enzyklopädisches Lexikon reveals the extent to which knowledge is shaped by the political, social, and cultural context in which it is produced. While the two simultaneously produced German encyclopedias might be similar in content when it comes to entries in the fields of technology and natural sciences, they differ greatly in the coverage of politics, history, society and culture. A side-by-side comparison thus offers fascinating discoveries and intriguing insights into the contextual nature of knowledge production.

Complimenting these competing texts in this spotlight collection is a selection of titles from the University Library System’s general collection relating to the cultural, social, and political history of Germany in the 20th century, with particular emphasis on the post-WWII division of the country into East and West. The collection also includes material relating to the country’s evolution after reunification in 1990. For further assistance, please contact subject librarian Dan Pennell at pennell@pitt.edu.

“Early on in Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston’s book for aspiring animators, The Illusion of Life, they say the following about their chosen medium: “Once an artist sees his drawings come to life on the screen, he will never again be quite satisfied with any other type of expression.”

The history of cinema is, ultimately, the history of animation. After all, cinema is, even in the era of digital dominance, a collection of still images viewed in sequence to create the illusion of motion--what is this if not animation? An “illusion of life,” as Thomas and Johnston describe it.

Herein we seek to capture a broader canon of animation that considers its many facets:

- the earliest forms of motion pictures

- avant-garde art

- short-form populist entertainment

- children’s entertainment

- an alternative mode of storytelling

- a medium that allows filmmakers to push the bounds of reality”

University of Pittsburgh Library System

Stark Media Collection

Located in Hillman Library, Media Services provides expertise and access to Hillman Library's film collections. The collection primarily supports classroom instruction across disciplines with an emphasis on Film Studies. Please see the
Stark Media Collection Statement
for more information.Most items in the collection are available for a two-week loan to University of Pittsburgh students, staff, and faculty with a valid Pitt ID. Please see our information about
Length of Loans
and Fines for more information on borrowing periods, overdue items, and replacement costs.

Requests & Reservations

Requesting Materials through Get-It

ULS films are housed across several locations, including our Oakland libraries and regional campus libraries. A significant portion of the collection is stored at the Thomas Boulevard Library, our secure, temperature-controlled off-site facility.
Placing a Get-It request is a quick and convenient way to access materials from the Stark Media Collection or any ULS library.

Start at
www.library.pitt.edu

Search for the title you are interested in

Click on the title from the results page

Sign into your Pitt Account

Click Request Item

Choose the location to deliver the item to

Click Send Request

You will receive a notification email when the item is read to pick up

Purchase Request Form

If we do not have the film(s) that you need in our collections, please use the
online form
to request that the ULS purchase media in streaming or physical format.

We will review your request, then contact you with available options. We cannot guarantee the availability of all requested formats, but will make every effort to fulfill requests as specified. Please note that the ULS prioritizes purchase requests intended for instructional or research use.

If you have questions about purchase requests for non-standard format options, or for specific editions of titles that are critical to the requirements of the course, please contact your
ULS Subject Specialist Librarian
for ordering assistance.

Reserve Request Form

Request that a film (ULS-owned or personal copy) be placed on reserve for students to view in Media Services at Hillman Library or to ensure it is available for a classroom screening. Placing films on reserve allows titles to be readily accessible for you and your students when needed.

Media Conversion

For questions about media duplication/digitization of physical media, please contact the
Center for Teaching and Learning
.

The Center for Teaching and Learning
Media Content Conversion Request Form

If the library owns a film in physical format, is there a way to get this uploaded to Canvas so students can watch it there?
Yes, we have a process!

Physical Media Regional Formats and other Troubleshooting

The ULS has a diverse film collection that includes a variety of formats (DVD, Blu-ray, VHS, 16mm film reels, and Laserdisc) sourced from around the world. Region specific-films are encoded in a way that requires specialized players in order to view the materials. Media Services has a variety of playback equipment in Hillman Library that is compatible with the region-specific materials in the collection.

PITTSBURGH –
The Pitt Panthers (5-3, 2-3 ACC) host Georgia Tech (2-5, 1-3 ACC) in primetime this Saturday at 7:30 PM on ESPN2.

Pitt and Georgia Tech meet for the 19th time in a series that dates to 1918. The Panthers lead the all-time series, 12-6, and have won seven of the past nine meetings. Pitt owns a 5-2 series record in Pittsburgh.

The Panthers defeated then No. 15 ranked Georgia Tech, 42-28, in Atlanta last season. Pitt has won five of the past six meetings and leads the ACC series, 7-4.

This Saturday's game against Georgia Tech will feature Hail to Heroes, sponsored by GBU Life and the Aldrich Foundation, honoring military members, veterans and first responders through on-field and in-game recognitions and patriotic elements celebrating those who serve. As part of their sponsorship, GBU Life and the Aldrich Foundation will sponsor the on-field and in-game recognition of heroes and veterans. Both organizations share a commitment to supporting active-duty personnel, veterans and their families, turning appreciation into action through GBU Life's Operation Reach Out, which delivers care packages to deployed service members, and the Aldrich Foundation's support of organizations such as Wreaths Across America and Joint Task Force K9s. Together, they help bring the community together to recognize service and make a lasting impact on those who have sacrificed for our country.

PITT vs. GEORGIA TECH

Oct. 31, 2026 • 7:30 PM

Acrisure Stadium (51,416/Natural Grass) • Pittsburgh, Pa.

ESPN2 • 93.7 The Fan • Pitt Panthers Radio Network

PittsburghPanthers.com • @Pitt_FB

GAME STORYLINES

• Pitt continues its 137th season of football Saturday when it hosts Georgia Tech. The Panthers enter the game at 5-3 overall and 2-3 in the ACC. Pitt is 4-1 at home this season.

• A victory Saturday would move Pitt to 6-3 overall and 3-3 in ACC play while securing bowl eligibility. The Panthers have held opponents to averages of 11.0 points and 48.0 rushing yards in five home games this season.

• Pitt owns a 7-2 record against Georgia Tech under
Pat Narduzzi
, including a 2-1 mark in Pittsburgh. The Panthers have won four of the past five meetings, with each victory coming by at least 10 points.

• Pitt produced 412 total yards and five offensive touchdowns in last season's victory at Georgia Tech.
Ja'Kyrian Turner
rushed for a career-high 201 yards and a touchdown, while
Braylan Lovelace
scored on a 100-yard interception return.

• Pitt ranks sixth in the ACC in total offense, averaging 444.3 yards per game, and third in passing offense at 290.8 yards per contest. The Panthers' 20 touchdown passes rank third in the conference, with 12 different players catching a touchdown pass.

•
Cataurus Hicks
caught five passes for a career-high 149 yards and a touchdown at Miami, surpassing his previous best of 135 yards at Boston College one week earlier. Hicks has totaled 284 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 10 catches over Pitt's past two games.

• Hicks leads Pitt with 31 receptions, 649 receiving yards, five touchdown catches and 772 all-purpose yards. He is the first Panther with at least three 100-yard receiving performances through the first eight games of a season since Jordan Addison in 2021.

•
Holden Geriner
passed for a career-high 268 yards and a touchdown without an interception at Miami. True freshman
Corey Dailey
completed all three of his passes for 66 yards, including a 49-yard touchdown to
Cam Sapp
, and has thrown a touchdown pass in each of his three collegiate appearances.

• True freshman
Damon Ferguson Jr.
leads Pitt with 477 rushing yards, averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Ferguson has produced 579 yards from scrimmage and five touchdowns through eight collegiate games, including a rushing touchdown at Miami.

• Pitt ranks second in the ACC in rushing defense, allowing 65.0 yards per game, and leads the conference in yards allowed per carry (2.2). The Panthers have held five of their first eight opponents below 100 rushing yards and four below 50.

• The Panthers lead the ACC with eight interceptions in conference play and rank second with nine overall.
Raion Strader
leads Pitt with three interceptions, including two red-zone picks at Boston College. Pitt ranks third in the ACC in fourth-down defense, stopping seven of 10 attempts.

•
Jaeden Moore
established career highs with five tackles, two sacks and 2.5 tackles for loss at Miami. Moore leads Pitt with 4.5 sacks and seven tackles for loss.
Cruce Brookins
leads the Panthers with 55 tackles and has recorded at least nine stops in four of Pitt's past five games.

•
Antonio Chadha
is 10-for-11 on field goals and 29-for-29 on extra points this season.
Gabe Russo's
59-yard punt at Miami established a season long, and he has produced 12 punts of at least 50 yards. Pitt has blocked 25 kicks under Narduzzi, including two field-goal attempts against Georgia Tech.

WHERE TO WATCH

National Television • ESPN2

Lowell Galindo (play-by-play)

Kirk Morrison (analyst)
